title: Building an offer that justifies a higher rate for Mobile hairdressing and barbering
audience: Mobile hairdressers and barbers who quote per cut, colour or visit, and want a price that reflects the travel, set-up and certainty they give a client at home.
learningOutcomes: Write a mobile hair or barbering offer with a clear outcome, time frame, client inputs and risk
Show travel, set-up and product costs as visible lines rather than hidden extras
Price service tiers on value and check each tier against cost and time

instruction.heading: A bad offer versus a good offer
instruction.body: “I can do a men’s cut” is a service. “I will cut and tidy your beard at your home in about 60 minutes, set up and clean down the area, and show you the finished line in a mirror before I pack up” is an offer. The client buys the finished look and the certainty that it will be done at their place, without a salon trip.

instruction.heading: The five parts of a mobile offer
instruction.body: Name the outcome in one sentence. Give the visit length, including set-up and clean-down. List what the client provides, such as a clear chair space, a mirror and a power point if you need one. Add one certainty element, such as a mirror check before you pack up. Set the risk you carry, such as a re-trim of an uneven line within a window you can keep. Write the scope and exclusions down, because a written quote becomes binding once it is accepted (business.gov.au, Prepare quotes). The research found no Australian operator price list for mobile hairdressing or barbering, so set the price from your own cost and time, not from a published figure.

instruction.heading: Reducing friction for the client
instruction.body: Make the booking, the access and the handover simple. Confirm the address, parking or entry, stairs and any pets before the visit. A client who does not have to travel, wait or ask questions is buying convenience, and each step you remove from their side supports a higher price.

instruction.heading: Guarantees, fix-first and consumer law
instruction.body: A guarantee must be something you can deliver and afford. For services, a business must be given a reasonable chance to fix a minor fault free of charge (Consumer Victoria, last updated 13 October 2023). That source does not set a length for the fix window, so you must choose one you can keep. A written warranty is an optional extra that sits on top of the consumer guarantees. A “no refunds” line does not override a customer’s rights for services (business.gov.au, Warranties and refunds). The research found no source on result claims for hair, such as colour condition or breakage, so do not publish one until you have evidence you can show.

instruction.heading: Service tiers and the total
instruction.body: Stepped packages work when each higher level adds something the client can see, such as a beard trim, a neck tidy or a finish. Jobber’s good-better-best examples, published May 2021 and updated 8 October 2024, use this pattern for trade services, although none of its examples is a hair service. One non-trade experiment found that reversing the order of three plans moved more buyers to the top plan, so test the order you present (INSEAD Knowledge, 2 October 2025). Show one clear total for the visit, with the travel charge as a separate line, and say whether GST is included (ACCC, Setting prices: what’s allowed). The ACCC says misleading statements about prices are prohibited. A 2015 ACCC drip-pricing case concerned online fees, so applying it to a mobile travel fee is an inference, not a finding.

procedure: Write the outcome for one service, such as a men’s cut at home, in one sentence a client would repeat.
Set the visit length, including set-up, clean-down and travel, and record how often you finish inside it.
List what the client must provide, and cut each step you can.
Add one certainty element, such as a mirror check at the chair, or a photo kept only with the client’s consent.
Decide the fix-first window and any warranty, and check that you can afford both.
Price the tiers from value, then check the total against your cost and time.

workedExamples.situation: A mobile barber loses jobs to a cheaper quote that says only “haircut” with a price. Clients ask what they will get, how long it takes and whether travel is included.
workedExamples.decisionPrompt: Rewrite the offer as service tiers, and show the price on the quote.
workedExamples.reasoning: Three tiers work: a cut only, a cut with a beard trim, and a cut with beard, neck tidy and finish. Each higher tier adds something the client can see. The visit length, the travel charge and the GST status appear as separate lines on the written quote, with one total. Each tier price comes from your own cost and time, as set in the BP-05 and HBM-12 lessons. This lesson gives no price. The clearer offer, rather than a lower hourly rate, is what supports the higher tier.

commonErrors.error: Promising a colour or chemical result that you cannot show
commonErrors.prevention: Describe the service and the steps you take. Do not state an outcome without evidence you can show.

commonErrors.error: Making a fix-first or re-trim promise you cannot keep
commonErrors.prevention: Set the window and the cost of the return visit before you publish the offer.

commonErrors.error: Adding a travel fee after the client has agreed to the price
commonErrors.prevention: Show the travel charge as its own line on the written quote before the visit.
State your fix-first policy and the client’s statutory rights in plain words, and keep both consistent.

safetyAndRegulatory.point: Registration and licence rules for hairdressing are set by each state and territory, and they differ. Victoria: councils register hairdressing premises under the Public Health and Wellbeing Act 2008. The council listing read did not say how mobile operators are treated, so ask your council. Northern Territory: a business paid for hairdressing must register (fee $91, no date shown). Queensland: hairdressing needs no licence, but the infection control guidelines apply. New South Wales: working as a hairdresser for a fee requires a qualification under the Hairdressers Act 2003, and a mobile operator working from a vehicle must notify the council for skin-penetration work. South Australia: the Hairdressers Act 1988 and the 2016 regulations apply, and recognition is needed without a prescribed qualification. Western Australia: shire notification or registration applies, but this was not verified. This lesson does not grant any licence.

Gap: no mobile-specific registration rule was confirmed in any state. Whether shaving counts as skin penetration in Victoria, New South Wales or Western Australia is not confirmed. The research did not check the rules for the Australian Capital Territory or Tasmania.

Consumer rules on prepaid work: a business must not take payment for a service it cannot supply within a reasonable time (Personal services guide, 2013). Gift card rules apply to most cards and vouchers sold on or after 1 November 2019, with a minimum three-year expiry. Memberships and prepaid packages are not clearly covered by the sources read, and South Australia has its own gift card law. Check the rules for your state before you sell a prepaid package.
Business guidance only. This lesson gives no tax advice. Check the tax treatment of your income with a registered tax agent.

qualityStandard: Every offer states the outcome, the visit length, the client inputs, the certainty element and the risk, in writing before the visit.
The travel charge and GST status appear on the quote as separate, checkable lines.
No result claim is published without evidence the business can show.
documentationEvidence: Written offer or tier sheet, with the date it was issued
Visit-length record, compared with the stated visit length
Record of any fix-first or warranty request and its outcome
summary: A good offer promises a named outcome, a time frame, client inputs, certainty and a fair guarantee.
Show the travel charge and GST as visible lines, so the higher price is easy to see.
Charge for value you can show, and check the price against your cost and time.

knowledgeChecks.question: Which part of a mobile offer does the customer buy?
What should a guarantee be?
options: Impossible to claim on in any case
Only for new customers and friends
Something you can deliver and afford

Jobber Academy, 'Good, Better, Best Pricing Examples', https://getjobber.com/academy/good-better-best-pricing-examples/, published May 2021, updated 8 October 2024. Supports: stepped packages. Older than 2022; trade examples are not hair services.
